Queue and Preview are flat buttons on the theme's base surface, #444444 in dark mode, their labels in the theme's text colour, a step lighter on hover, doing what the send menu's options of those names do, with tooltips saying that Queue queues the prompt even while the harness is free, and that Preview previews the compiled prompt. 22:On the Code tab, while the send menu offers "Send to task", as its options say, the running task being a Code task in the code lane, the send button reads "Send to task" instead of "Queue", its tooltip saying it sends the prompt to the running task, and it and <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) send to the task just as that option does, rather than queueing. The Queue button and the menu's "Queue" still queue the prompt. While the code lane is busy any other way, a Freeform task running, a Code task whose harness can't be fed more, a task building or compiling, or the previous tasks expanded over its output, the button reads "Queue" and the prompt queues, as ever. 28:## Send Options
30:### Split Button
32:The send button is a split button: the send or queue button itself, and joined to its right, a narrow half with a chevron that opens a menu of other ways to send the prompt, above the button, its right edge lined up with the button's. The chevron half is disabled whenever the send half is, and while a preview shows, and its tooltip says it shows more ways to send, with its shortcut.
34:### Keyboard
38:### Options
44:- "Send to task", with a send icon, only while a task is running with a harness that can be fed more, as the [HarnessIntegration](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration) says, and its output is shown, the previous tasks not expanded over it; never on the Ask tab, where a question runs on its own. It sends what is typed, and what is attached, to the running task instead of queueing it, as the [PromptSending](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending) says, and clears the input as sending does. On the Code tab, while it is offered for a Code task running in the code lane, it is also what the send button and <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) do, as the description says; on the other tabs they still queue
46:## Editing Queued
48:Editing a queued prompt, from the queue of the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor), sets aside the prompt being written, its attachments, and the selected tab, and puts the queued prompt's text in the input, its attachments above it, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of the text. Above the attachments, a row with a pencil icon reads "Editing queued prompt N", its place in the queue, and at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to save · Esc to cancel" (with ⌘ on macOS). The send button reads "Save", its tooltip saying it saves the queued prompt, and the send menu isn't offered.
49:Everything in the input works as ever while editing, tabs included. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or Save, saves the edit, in the tab selected then, and <Escape>, when nothing else in the input takes it, cancels it. Either way, the prompt that was set aside comes back just as it was. Saving an empty prompt isn't possible, just as sending one isn't. Editing another queued prompt meanwhile first cancels the edit in progress; so does switching projects.
51:## Up Arrow
57:## Preview
59:Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building the spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows what the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with, at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up to 40% of the window's height, and scrolls beyond that. The tabs, attachments, and send button stay as they are.
60:The preview has keyboard focus. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or the send button, sends the prompt just as sending from the text input would, and the chat input goes back to an empty text input. <Escape> goes back to the text input with the prompt and attachments as they were, the cursor where it was. Switching tabs while previewing goes back to the text input too, since the prompt would compile differently.

I made the change, but I couldn't compile or run it. The build reads `.suspense/system-prompts/*.md`, and that directory gives "Permission denied" even outside the sandbox, so `cargo test` fails before it reaches my code.

**What changed:** on the Code tab, when the send menu offers "Send to task" and the running task is a Code task, the send button and Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) now send to that task instead of queueing it. In that state the button reads "Send to task", with the tooltip "Send to the running task (Ctrl+Enter)". The Queue button and the menu's "Queue" still queue. The new check is in `src/chat_input.rs`, and `PromptMode` tells the input on each render whether the latest task is a Code task.

**What stays the same:**
- Every other way the code lane can be busy still shows "Queue" and queues.
- The other tabs (Chain, Spec, Freeform, Ask) never send to the task this way.
- While a queued prompt is being edited, Ctrl+Enter still saves the edit.
- Sending from the preview does the same as sending from the text box, as the spec says.

**Test:** I extended `send_to_task_is_offered_while_a_task_can_be_sent_more` to cover these cases, but it hasn't been run.

**Possible layout problem:** "Send to task" is much longer than "Queue". With the send icon and the chevron, it may not fit the 108px button column, so it could get cut off or spill over. I couldn't render the app to check. If it doesn't fit, the column needs to be wider or the label shorter, and the spec has to agree to either one.

I didn't find anything where the spec and the prompt disagree.
